Inverse Standard Normal

z from a central probability. FMLA 04/05 only go the other way. 156 bytes.

keys
MODE→6→2

FMLA 04/05 map z → probability. This WebCal DSE-accurate inverse listing maps p = P(0 ≤ Z ≤ x) → x using the exam table plus linear interpolation, so the digits match the HKEAA book. Prompt is p with 0 < p < 0.5. Table hits (two decimal z) print as a terminating two-decimal x. In-between values print the interpolated z; RCL A, B are the two table probabilities and RCL Y, M are the two z-grid points for the written working.

note

156 bytes of the shared 680-byte pool. Create the slot in COMP. Type ? → : ◢ Goto Lbl If Then from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).

formula
P(0≤Z≤x)=p

basic
?→C:ln(1−4C²:Fix 2:Rnd(√(−Ans−8+√(Ans²−9Ans+64→M:M→Y:Fix 4:Lbl 0:B→A:2÷(2+.4633M:Rnd(.5−E−4e^(−.5M²)Ans(1274−1422Ans+Ans²(7107−7266Ans+5307Ans²→B:(M=Y)+(A=B⇒.01−.02(B>C)M+⇒Goto 0:Norm 1:Y+(Y−M)(C−A)÷(A−B

Example 1: P(0 ≤ Z ≤ x) = 0.3907

Question: Use this program to solve the case: P(0 ≤ Z ≤ x) = 0.3907.

Given: This p sits on the printed table, so x is exactly two decimals.

  1. 0.3907 EXE
  2. Display 1.23

Example 2: P(0 ≤ Z ≤ x) = 0.3 (needs interpolation)

Question: Use this program to solve the case: P(0 ≤ Z ≤ x) = 0.3 (needs interpolation).

Given: After the run, RCL A ≈ 0.2995, RCL B ≈ 0.3023, RCL Y = 0.84, RCL M = 0.85.

  1. 0.3 EXE
  2. Display ≈ 0.841785714
  3. Those four recalls are the interpolation lines you write in the script

Example 3 (edge): p outside (0, 0.5)

Question: Use this program to solve the case: p outside (0, 0.5).

Given: Left tail, two-tail, or p ≥ 0.5 must be rewritten first.

  1. P(Z ≤ a) = 0.9 → central slab is 0.4, then run 0.4; the printed x is a
  2. P(Z ≥ a) = 0.1 is the same 0.4 slab
  3. p = 0 or p ≥ 0.5 → Math ERROR or a stuck loop. Do not enter 0.5
note

Fix 2, Fix 4, Norm 1 and Rnd( are the display-format commands — enter them from SET UP (SHIFT MODE) while editing. E is EXP, so E−4 is 10⁻⁴. e^( is SHIFT eˣ. p > 0.4973 can hit a multi-z table clash; AC then RCL M is the fallback. Source: WebCal standardnormal_6 program I.
